content:
**Key observations from the image:**

- Most of the plant has healthy, vibrant green leaves in the upper canopy
- Lower canopy leaves are yellowing, turning tan/brown, and drooping downward toward the soil
- The dying lower leaves appear uniformly yellowed/tan rather than showing distinct spotting patterns
- No visible white mold, powdery coating, or obvious fruiting bodies
- Upper leaves are completely unaffected

**Reasoning:**

The classic bottom-up pattern of lower canopy defoliation while the upper canopy remains fully green is the hallmark of **Septoria brown spot**. This disease starts in the lower canopy under moist conditions, causes leaves to yellow and drop, and progressively moves upward. The tan/brown, drooping lower leaves with general yellowing match this progression.

SDS was also considered (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis), but SDS typically shows a more distinct interveinal pattern with veins remaining green. The lower leaves here appear more uniformly yellowed. Downy mildew was considered but lacks the tufts of fungal growth on leaf undersides. Phytophthora would show chocolate-brown stem discoloration from the soil line up.
